title: Who Leads and Who Collects:Algorithmic Collusion in Markets of Heterogeneous Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.11256v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evidence that pricing algorithms collude comes from markets in which every seller runs the same algorithm. We ask what happens when they do not. Four language models from four providers, each at its cheapest tier, price in a four-firm logit Bertrand market without communication, in every homogeneous, two-by-two and fully mixed composi- tion (11 cells, 20 runs, 200 periods). Collusion is a property of the model: Claude and Gemini markets reach 72 to 79 percent of the monopoly rent, DeepSeek markets 24 percent, and GPT markets none, though GPT prices drift above the monopoly level rather than toward competition. Mixing does not reduce collusion by itself. translated_title: 《谁主导、谁获利：异构语言模型市场中的算法合谋》
translated_abstract: 有证据表明定价算法会合谋，但这些证据来自每个卖家都运行相同算法的市场。我们探究当卖家运行不同算法时会发生什么。来自四家提供商的四个语言模型，各自使用其最低价格档位，在一个四企业logit Bertrand市场中定价，全程无通信，覆盖所有同质、二对二及完全混合的组合（11个单元格、20次运行、200个周期）。研究发现合谋是模型本身的一种属性：Claude和Gemini市场达到垄断租金的72%至79%，DeepSeek市场为24%，GPT市场则完全没有，不过GPT的价格是漂移到垄断水平之上而非趋向竞争水平。模型混合本身并不能减少合谋。包含Gemini的市场（其开盘价最高且最终稳定在最高价）比构成它们的同质市场更具合谋性；包含Claude的市场（其开盘较低并跟随对手降价）合谋性则较低；而只有完全混合市场显著……
tldr: 该研究首次在异构语言模型市场中验证了算法合谋是模型自身的属性而非“相同算法”的产物——Claude和Gemini主导的市场合谋程度最高（达垄断租金的72-79%），GPT则不合谋，且混合不同模型并不必然抑制合谋，含Gemini的市场更易合谋而含Claude的市场更趋于竞争。
en_tdlr: Algorithmic collusion is shown to be a property of the language model itself rather than identical algorithms—Claude and Gemini markets reach 72-79% of monopoly rents while GPT shows none, and mixing heterogeneous models does not reduce collusion, with Gemini-containing markets being more collusive and Claude-containing markets less so.
